chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites Surah al-Mu'minun, Allah seals for him with happiness, and if one is habitual in reciting it every Friday, his abode will be in the highest Paradise with the prophets and the messengers.

key_terms.الْفِرْدَوْسِ الْأَعْلَی: Al-Firdaws al-A'la, the highest level of Paradise
key_terms.سُورَهَ الْمُؤْمِنِینَ: Surah al-Mu'minun (The Believers), the 23rd chapter of the Quran
key_terms.مُدْمِنَ: Habitual, one who does something consistently or frequently

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah al-Mu'minun every Friday?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this narration emphasizes the transformative power of consistent devotion, linking the recitation of Surah al-Mu'minun to divine sealing of happiness (sa'adah). The specific mention of Friday highlights the day's significance in Shia tradition as a time for spiritual renewal, promising the highest tier of Paradise (Al-Firdaws) among the prophets and messengers for those who make this recitation a habitual practice.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan b. al-Hussain b. Abi al-’Ala from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

Whoever recites Surah Mominoon, Allah completes for him the greatness of virtues and auspiciousness and if someone recites Surah Mominoon every Friday regularly, his position would be in the high garden of Paradise where he would be with the prophets and messengers.
